Bench: P.Sree Sudha
The Honourable Smt. Justice P.Sree Sudha
 M.A.C.M.A.No.3153 of 2009
J U D G M E N T:

This Motor Accident Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act,
1988 against the Judgment and Decree dated 02.01.2009 passed in O.P.No.298 of 2004 (old O.P.No.4 of 2004) passed by the learned Chairman, Motor Vehicles Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-II Additional District Judge, Nalgonda at Suryapet.

entities.text: Motor Vehicles Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-II Additional District Judge, Nalgonda at Suryapet
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 02. The Original Petition in O.P.No.298 of 2004 (old O.P.No.4 of 2004) was filed by appellants/petitioners claiming compensation of Rs.3,00,000/- for death of Gundagani Yellaiah (here-in-after referred as 'deceased'), who died in the motor vehicle accident occurred on 10.11.2003.
Appellant No.1 is the wife, appellant No.2 and 3 are children and appellant No.4 is the mother of the deceased.
The trial Court after considering the arguments of both sides, granted compensation only to an extent of Rs.1,87,500/-.
Aggrieved by the said Judgment and decree, they preferred the present appeal.
03. As the present appeal is preferred only for enhancement of the compensation amount granted by the trial Court, this Court is not going into other details.

04. The learned Counsel for the appellants / petitioners contended that as on the date of accident,
the age of the deceased was 38 years and he was lorry cleaner and earning Rs.4,000/- per month.
Therefore, requested the Court to modify the award passed by the trial Court.
05. Admittedly, the deceased was lorry cleaner.

Considering the age and occupation of the deceased,
this Court finds that it is just and reasonable to take the salary of the deceased as Rs.4,000/-, as such his annual income would be Rs.48,000/- (Rs.4000 x 12).
06.

As per the guidelines of the Hon'ble Apex Court in dictum of Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation,1 if the deceased was married, 1/4th of his income has to be deducted as there are 4 dependents i.e., 12,000/- towards his personal expenses.

entities.text: Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation,1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the annual income of the deceased after deducting personal expenses would come to Rs.36,000/- per annum (Rs.48,000- 12,000=Rs.36,000/-) and the Hon'ble Apex Court in the dictum of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi2, held that the future prospects of income of the self-employed deceased shall also be included in determination of the compensation.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, considering the age of the Gundagoni Vijayalaxmi And 3 Others vs M.Subba Rao And 2 Others on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181710146/
1 deceased, 40% of the income i.e., Rs.14,400/- has to be added towards future prospects and thus the amount would become Rs.50,400/- (Rs.36,000 + Rs.14,400 = Rs.50,400/-).

entities.text: Gundagoni Vijayalaxmi And 3 Others vs M.Subba Rao And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This sum if multiplied with the multiplier 15 applicable to the age of the deceased is 40 years, it would come to Rs.07,56,000/- (Rs.50,400 X 15 = Rs.07,56,000/-).

Thus, appellants are entitled to Rs.07,56,000/-
under the head 'Loss of Dependency'.

Besides, appellants are also entitled for compensation under 'conventional heads' as prescribed in the dictum of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi, i.e., Rs.15,000/- towards loss of Estate and Rs.15,000/- towards funeral charges and Rs.40,000/- to the first appellant towards spousal consortium.
08.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, the Hon'ble Supreme Court, by reiterating the comprehensive interpretation of 'consortium' given in the authority of Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & others3, and in the authority between United India Insurance Company Limited vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur and others4, fortified that the amounts for loss of consortium shall be awarded to the children who lose the care and protection of their parents as 'parental consortium' and to the parents as, 'filial consortium' for the loss of their grown-up children, to compensate their agony, love and affection, care and companionship of deceased children.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: United India Insurance Company Limited vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur and others4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, it is just and reasonable to award (2018) 18 SCC 130 (2020) 9 SCC 644 Rs.40,000/- each to appellants No.2 and 3 as parental consortium and Rs.40,000/- to appellant No.4 towards filial consortium.

09. Therefore, appellants/petitioners are entitled for the compensation in the following terms:
1. Loss of dependency Rs.07,56,000/-
2. Conventional heads Rs.70,000/-
3. Parental Consortium for children Rs.80,000/-
@ Rs.40,000/- each 4. Filial Consortium for parent @ Rs.40,000/-
Rs.40,000/-

10. Accordingly, this Motor Accident Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is allowed by enhancing the compensation amount from Rs.01,87,500/- to Gundagoni Vijayalaxmi And 3 Others vs M.Subba Rao And 2 Others on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181710146/
2 Rs.09,46,000/- (Rupees Nine Lakhs Fourty Six Thousand only) with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of filing the petition till date of realization.

sentences.text: Respondent shall deposit the entire amount within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a copy of this Judgment.
On such deposit, all the appellants are permitted to withdraw the said amount along with interest accrued on it.
Out of total compensation amount, appellants No.2 to 4 are entitled to Rs.50,000/- each and appellant No.1 is entitled to remaining amount.
Appellants are directed to pay the deficit Court fee on the enhanced amount.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
